title: rapid-integration-mini-manual-for-embedded-sdks
content:
Purpose:
This is a tightly scoped mini-manual aimed at engineers embedding Redwood SDKs into product flows (mobile/web/backend). Goal: a minimal, reproducible path from repo -> running example -> validated telemetry in under 20 minutes. This is intentionally terse: checklists, common pitfalls, and a canonical failure-mode triage section.

Audience:
- Product engineers implementing a first integration
- SDK reviewers/internal QA
- Solutions engineers running quick demos

What this doc is NOT:
- Not a full API reference (see repo README and docs.redwood.ai).
- Not an exhaustive security guide (see security-and-compliance drive).

Quick TL;DR (5–20 minute path)
1) Clone minimal sample: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground && cd sdk-playground/minimal-embed
2) Copy API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_test_key (use secrets manager in prod)
3) Install: pnpm install (or pip install -r requirements.txt)
4) Run sample server: node server.js or python app.py
5) Load demo UI or run curl to exercise generate/chat/embedding endpoints
6) Confirm telemetry: open /_health/telemetry or check Sentry/Datadog events for sample-run tag

Starter checklist (tick during run):
- [ ] Repo builds locally without extra flags
- [ ] Sample uses environment-based config (no hardcoded keys)
- [ ] SDK client initialized once per worker/process
- [ ] Telemetry event emitted on first request with sample-run tag
- [ ] SDK errors surfaced but do not crash caller by default (human-friendly error mapping)

Opinionated integration patterns (recommended)
- Initialization: central client factory (server-side) that injects credentials via env + optional vault. Avoid per-request construction.
- Concurrency: for backend workers, use a singleton client with shared connection pool (JS: module-scoped; Python: process-global).
- Request shaping: prefer batched embedding calls where possible; use time-window batching with max-size guardrails (see examples).
- Fallbacks: implement a thin circuit-breaker that returns cached or degraded content when latency exceeds 300ms for sync calls.

Minimal config example (JS pseudo):
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: process.env.REDWOOD_REGION || 'us-west-2', telemetryNamespace: 'product-demo' });

// use client across handlers
async function handle(req) {
  try {
    const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-embed-1', prompt: req.body.prompt });
    return json(200, resp);
  } catch (e) {
    // map common errors for UI
    return json(500, { error: e.message.replace(/Token.*/g, '[redacted]') });
  }
}

Common failure modes and triage (fast):
- "401 / invalid key" -> check env, ensure using sandbox vs prod keys, confirm service account binding in Private deployments.
- "Connection refused / ENETUNREACH" -> local proxy misconfigured or VPC egress blocked; temporarily set REDWOOD_REGION to hosted region for testing.
- "High tail latency" -> run local profilers; check sample sequence length is artificially high; enable batching to reduce token wait.
- "Duplicate calls" -> likely multiple client instances per request; add logs to detect new client construction events.

Telemetry & instrumentation (must-haves for a demo):
- Emit event: sdk.integration.started with fields: sample_id, user_id (pseudonymized), sdk_version.
- Emit event: sdk.integration.error with error_kind, http_status, upstream_model.
- Sample SLO to validate: 95th latency under 400ms for single-turn generation in demo environment.
- Add counters for request_count, batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate (if using prefix caching).

Smoke test matrix (scriptable):
- smoke-basic.sh: start, call /generate with short prompt, assert 200 and contains text.
- smoke-telemetry.sh: run sample then query telemetry endpoint to assert sdk.integration.started exists in last 5m.
- smoke-fallback.sh: simulate backend slowdown (sleep) and assert circuit-breaker path responds with cached payload.

UX copy snippets (for product teams)
- Loading indicator: "Thinking... (we're checking for fast answers)"
- Retry messaging: "Sorry — temporary timeout. Try again or continue in background."

Security notes (short):
- Never commit API keys. Use platform secret store mapped to CI and runtime.
- For Private deployments, validate cert fingerprint and KMS access before onboarding.
- Redact PII from telemetry; use hashing for user identifiers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we standardize a single sample-run telemetry tag across SDKs? (ticket: SDK-120)
- Add an example mobile wrapper (iOS/Android) that demonstrates background model calls without blocking UI (assign Rafael).
- Validate binary-size impact of including the full client in mobile builds; create benchmark.

Links & references:
- Minimal sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground/tree/main/minimal-embed
- Deployment checklist (private): docs:redwood/private-deploy-checklist (internal)
- CI job: .github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml (related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground/pull/42)

Notes to self:
- Keep examples as single-file runnable assets (no monorepo navigation for first-run).
- Capture screenshots of telemetry UI for demo docs.
- Follow up with SRE on recommended default circuit-breaker thresholds for Dedicated customers.

Appendix: quick run commands
# Node
pnpm install && REDWOOD_API_KEY=$KEY node server.js
# Python
pip install -r requirements.txt && REDWOOD_API_KEY=$KEY python app.py

End of mini-manual.

(If this doc lands well, we should fold key checklist pieces into the main quickstart and add an "integration-run" badge for repos.)
